document.title: The t-wise Independence of Substitution-Permutation Networks

candidate.title: t-Wise Independence of AES for t > 2
candidate.subtitle: Pairwise is done; the next level has no proof and one cautionary counterexample nearby
candidate.one_line: For every t > 2 and every eps > 0 there is a round count r such that r-round AES with independent round keys is eps-close to t-wise independent.
candidate.status_note: Named by the source as the first of 'the two outstanding open problems that come of this work'. It proves almost pairwise independence (t = 2) for multi-round AES with independent round keys, and an existential t-wise result for key-alternating ciphers with most permutations, but nothing for concrete AES beyond t = 2.
candidate.progress_note: Theorem 3.14 gives 6r-round AES 2^{r-1}(0.472)^r-close to pairwise independence. Appendix B gives an attack on 4-wise independence for the width-1 key-alternating cipher with the same patched-inverse S-box, at modest round counts.

parameters.meaning: the independence order; the open regime is t > 2
round count, the quantity a resolution must bound as a function of t and eps

candidate.why_interesting: The next rung above the pairwise results that this line has established, on a real cipher, with a genuine nearby counterexample constraining the shape of any proof.
candidate.why_clean: One cipher, one order of independence, one key model stated explicitly.

quotes.quote: the two outstanding open problems that come of this work are (a) to prove t-wise independence of multi-round AES with independent round keys, for t > 2; and (b) to formalize and prove security against algebraic attacks.
understanding the precise role of key schedules is an important open problem.
We show that for a modest number of rounds r
Sufficiently strong (almost) pairwise independence already suffices to resist (truncated) differential attacks and linear cryptanalysis

check.notes: The open problem is verbatim on page 7 but is named without quantifiers: no t, no eps, no target round count. The quantifier structure in the conjecture -- for every t and eps, some finite r -- is this statement's choice and is flagged as such in a dedicated remark, along with the note that a resolution should report the dependence r(t,eps). The second correction is contextual: the source's own Appendix B refutes the width-1 specialization of the claim at modest round counts, which is recorded as an obstruction rather than buried, together with the reason (Carlitz) that it does not refute the conjecture itself.
